topics.title: Chapter overview
topics.summary: Systems programming requires knowing which assumptions the language actually permits. Undefined behavior, unspecified choices, and implementation-defined properties are not interchangeable categories. This chapter keeps the normal executable fully defined and places a deliberately invalid sanitizer experiment in a separate optional file. A clean run is useful evidence, but the central goal is to remove invalid assumptions rather than depend on one machine’s tolerance.

topics.title: 8.1.1 Understanding Undefined Behavior
topics.summary: Undefined behavior means the language imposes no requirements on that execution after the relevant violation. Examples include certain out-of-bounds accesses, signed overflow, invalid object-lifetime use, and unsynchronized conflicting ordinary accesses. It is not a guaranteed exception or a predictable wraparound rule.

rich: Undefined behavior means the language imposes no requirements on that execution after the relevant violation. Examples include certain out-of-bounds accesses, signed overflow, invalid object-lifetime use, and unsynchronized conflicting ordinary accesses. It is not a guaranteed exception or a predictable wraparound rule.

blocks.text: Compilers optimize under the assumption that a well-formed program follows applicable semantic requirements. Consequently, undefined behavior can affect surrounding code in surprising ways, not merely the single instruction a programmer expected to fail. Repair the source contract and validate inputs before dangerous operations rather than using observed output as proof that the violation is harmless.

blocks.text: Undefined behavior means the language imposes no requirements on the result of the invalid execution. It is not a standardized exception, a guaranteed crash, or a promise that the program will continue with a wrapped value. A test that happens to print the expected result does not establish a valid contract for the same source under another build or input.

blocks.text: Signed integer overflow is a useful example because the invalid operation can look like ordinary arithmetic. Computing a + b and then checking whether the result exceeded the type’s limit does not prevent overflow: the addition has already been evaluated. The worked helper instead compares operands against safe boundary expressions before adding them. Prevention must occur before the operation whose validity is in question. (LANG, NUMERIC)

blocks.text: Lifetime and bounds defects have the same ordering problem. Checking a pointer after dereferencing it does not make the dereference safe. Catching a C++ exception around an invalid access does not turn arbitrary native memory faults into ordinary exceptions. A pointer can be nonnull yet refer to an expired object or insufficient range. Validation must establish the actual preconditions, not merely the easiest property to test.

Validation must establish the actual preconditions, not merely the easiest property to test.

blocks.text: Undefined behavior also affects optimization reasoning. The compiler can transform code under the assumption that a valid execution obeys the language’s rules. A programmer who relies on a signed overflow check that itself overflows may find the check removed or rearranged in a way that seems surprising. The repair is to express a valid calculation, not to demand that optimization preserve an invalid intermediate result.

blocks.text: Avoid executing an invalid version merely to “see what happens” when inspection already identifies the defect. Controlled diagnostic demonstrations can be educational, but they should be isolated, clearly labeled, and excluded from ordinary tests. The normal companion programs are written to satisfy their stated bounds and ownership contracts. A negative sanitizer run is evidence that a particular diagnostic detected a particular exercised defect, not a license to use undefined behavior elsewhere.

topics.title: 8.1.2 Understanding Unspecified and Implementation-Defined Behavior
topics.summary: Unspecified behavior allows one of several permitted choices without requiring the implementation to document which choice occurs. Implementation-defined behavior requires the implementation to document its choice. Properties such as the signedness of plain char depend on the implementation, while some evaluation-order choices remain unspecified under applicable language rules.

rich: Unspecified behavior allows one of several permitted choices without requiring the implementation to document which choice occurs. Implementation-defined behavior requires the implementation to document its choice. Properties such as the signedness of plain char depend on the implementation, while some evaluation-order choices remain unspecified under applicable language rules.

blocks.text: These categories are not automatically bugs when the program remains correct for every permitted outcome it relies on. Portability fails when code assumes one choice without stating or checking it. Record platform-dependent requirements with traits, static assertions, or configuration checks, and avoid presenting one compiler’s observed result as a universal language rule.
rich: These categories are not automatically bugs when the program remains correct for every permitted outcome it relies on. Portability fails when code assumes one choice without stating or checking it. Record platform-dependent requirements with traits, static assertions, or configuration checks, and avoid presenting one compiler’s observed result as a universal language rule.

blocks.text: Implementation-defined behavior involves a choice the implementation documents. The signedness of plain char is a familiar example. A program can inspect that property and adapt, or avoid depending on it by choosing an explicitly signed or unsigned type where the distinction matters. The important point is that the choice is not arbitrary on every execution; it belongs to the implementation contract.
rich: Implementation-defined behavior involves a choice the implementation documents. The signedness of plain

is a familiar example. A program can inspect that property and adapt, or avoid depending on it by choosing an explicitly signed or unsigned type where the distinction matters. The important point is that the choice is not arbitrary on every execution; it belongs to the implementation contract.

blocks.text: Unspecified behavior permits more than one allowed result without requiring the implementation to document one fixed choice. Evaluation order can expose such freedom in otherwise-valid code. When independent function arguments have observable effects, their allowed ordering may not be the order a reader assumes from left-to-right typography. Write separate statements when a particular order is part of the intended behavior rather than relying on a convenient observation.
rich: Unspecified behavior permits more than one allowed result without requiring the implementation to document one fixed choice. Evaluation order can expose such freedom in otherwise-valid code. When independent function arguments have observable effects, their allowed ordering may not be the order a reader assumes from left-to-right typography. Write separate statements when a particular order is part of the intended behavior rather than relying on a convenient observation.

blocks.text: Neither category is automatically a bug. A program can be correct when all permitted outcomes satisfy its requirements. The defect arises when the application silently assumes a narrower outcome than the language or platform guarantees. A test that accepts either allowed ordering may be appropriate for demonstrating the language rule; an application requiring one ordering should express it explicitly.
rich: Neither category is automatically a bug. A program can be correct when all permitted outcomes satisfy its requirements. The defect arises when the application silently assumes a narrower outcome than the language or platform guarantees. A test that accepts either allowed ordering may be appropriate for demonstrating the language rule; an application requiring one ordering should express it explicitly.

blocks.text: Keep defined unsigned wrap separate from both categories. Unsigned arithmetic has modular behavior under its type’s rules, but that does not make every wrapping calculation sensible for a resource limit. A length that wraps to a small allocation followed by a large copy can still cause a serious bounds defect. Defined arithmetic is not the same as a correct application algorithm.

blocks.text: A useful portability record has three columns: required invariant, implementation choice relied upon, and evidence for that choice. For example, an octet protocol can require eight-bit bytes, check the lab assumption, and isolate it in the codec. A native file-descriptor wrapper can explicitly target Linux close behavior. This is more honest than labeling code portable while embedding undocumented assumptions throughout it. The goal is controlled dependence, not the impossible elimination of every platform-specific decision from systems software.

topics.title: 8.2.1 Using Compiler Warnings
topics.summary: Strong warnings can expose narrowing, suspicious comparisons, shadowing, missing returns, and other likely defects. Warning sets and diagnostic quality vary by compiler and version. Enable a useful baseline and review each finding rather than disabling a broad category to make a build appear clean.

blocks.text: A warning-free program can still contain serious undefined behavior, and some warnings identify a risk rather than a proven defect. Treat diagnostics as engineering signals that require interpretation. Keep intentional conversions explicit and justify their range at the boundary, so the code communicates why an operation is safe instead of merely silencing the warning.

Keep intentional conversions explicit and justify their range at the boundary, so the code communicates why an operation is safe instead of merely silencing the warning.

blocks.text: Warnings are compiler observations about suspicious or nonconforming code, not a complete proof system. Enable strong warnings early so newly introduced issues are visible against a clean baseline. A warning-free build is useful evidence, but it does not establish the absence of lifetime defects, data races, protocol errors, or invalid input paths that the compiler cannot infer.

blocks.text: Read the diagnostic’s location and reasoning. A conversion warning may reveal a real loss of range, or it may identify a deliberate bounded conversion whose precondition should be made explicit. Do not silence every warning with a cast. A cast changes the expression’s type treatment; it does not prove the runtime value fits. Validate or redesign the interface, then use a cast only where the checked relationship is clear.

blocks.text: Different compilers can diagnose different aspects of the same program. Building with GCC and Clang provides two front-end perspectives, but both can use the same standard-library implementation. Record that distinction in verification reports. Two compiler names do not imply two independent libraries, operating systems, or architectures. A portability claim must describe the actual matrix rather than count tool names as interchangeable evidence.

blocks.text: Treat warnings in generated or third-party code deliberately. A project can enforce strict warnings on its own targets while managing external code through separate policies. Global suppression can hide new defects in application code; global error treatment can make dependency upgrades difficult for reasons unrelated to the application’s correctness. Target-based build settings make those choices visible.
